clue.text: Shyness of daughter, given that I had put in barrier

parts.note: given that means if

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is set inside the barrier word

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A girl's timidity is explained by her being fenced in.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffidence is a lack of self-confidence, a close synonym of shyness.

clue.text: Tendency to flap like wings a tiny distance is restricted

parts.note: alar is the adjective meaning of or like wings

indicators.note: restricted tells us the short word is held in by the distance abbreviation

parts.note: a millimetre, abbreviated mm, is a tiny distance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird flapping its wings only moves a tiny distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' here means a state of panic, not wing-beating, though the surface plays on both.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a panic, and alarmism is a habit of raising needless panic.

clue.text: Part of formal outfit that needs little work put in

indicators.note: put in tells us the work is inserted into the word that

parts.note: taken as written
op, short for opus, is a little word for a work

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up formally takes little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is worn as part of morning dress or white-tie formal wear.

clue.text: One leader in mosque, a male

definitions.text: One leader in mosque, a male

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: leader in means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A description of a man who leads worship at a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the man who leads prayers in a mosque.

clue.text: Things added in glues, securing better, ultimately

indicators.note: securing tells us the glue word holds the picked letter inside

parts.note: cements are glues, as verbs or nouns

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Advice on additives that make adhesives work better.
explanation.definitionFit: Increments are small amounts added on, as in pay rises.

clue.text: Scraps not even soldiers take seriously at first

parts.note: a number not even is odd
men is a common term for soldiers

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a squabble don't take matters seriously at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover bits and pieces, which is what scraps are.

clue.text: A name selected at random for boy

parts.note: to draw is to select by lot, so drew means selected at random

explanation.surface: A child's name picked out of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At random' looks like an anagram signal but belongs with 'selected' as the definition of drew.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is a common given name for a male child, so the boy could be one of that name.

clue.text: City with cathedral next to river bank

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Describes a cathedral city standing beside a river bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to rely on it.

clue.text: Is no male disposed to admit female here?

indicators.note: to admit tells us the rearranged letters let one more in
disposed means arranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a misogynist would let a woman visit some place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'here' points to a place the whole clue describes; it also sets up 16 across, since the island named is a man-isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is the place pointed to; the clue's question describes it in a playful way.

clue.text: This poet repeatedly agreed to press for payment, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment

explanation.surface: A poet who kept agreeing to chase debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly agreed' alludes to 'Done!' (agreed), which Donne famously punned on his own name again and again in 'A Hymn to God the Father'; the poet's name is said like dun.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was the English metaphysical poet.

clue.text: 14 across quoting 10 after 16

parts.note: the title of a novel by the writer at 14 across, taken from the passage of the poet at 10 that follows the famous line at 16

explanation.surface: A cross-reference describing a novel's title source.
explanation.walkthrough: Hemingway's novel takes its title from Donne's Meditation XVII, which continues after 'No man is an island' with 'send not to know for whom the bell tolls'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hemingway novel's title is a quotation from the Donne meditation following that line.

clue.text: Note cut by railway, so start another union

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a remark is a note or comment

explanation.surface: A memo about railway cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Union here is a marriage, not a trade union as the railway surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To remarry is to enter a new marriage, a marriage being a union.

clue.text: Democratic split resulting in powerless movement

parts.note: a rift is a split

explanation.surface: A party schism leaves a political movement impotent.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift is motion carried by currents with no power of one's own.

clue.text: Writer represented as enigma — why?

indicators.note: represented as says the letters are shown in a new form

explanation.surface: Why is an author a puzzle?
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist.

clue.text: People hiking, often, left in shelter so arranged

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
arranged means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Hikers left in a shelter organised that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth hostellers are often walkers using hostels on hikes.

clue.text: For example, klutz in pantry 'id dish I smashed

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A clumsy person broke a dish in the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h in 'id (hid) is part of the run; klutz, a clumsy person, is a word from Yiddish.
explanation.definitionFit: Klutz is a word English took from Yiddish, so it is an example of a Yiddish borrowing.

clue.text: What 10 wrote, disproved by 9?

parts.note: a famous line by the poet at 10, jokingly refuted by the place at 9, which is literally an island named for a man

explanation.surface: A cross-reference joke about a poet being proved wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne's line says no person stands alone; the Isle of Man is an island that is 'Man', so it seems to disprove him.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Donne's best-known line from Meditation XVII.

clue.text: Home for flier crossing region in part of Asia

indicators.note: crossing means the home word spans across the region word

parts.note: a nest is a home for a bird, a flier
an area is a region

explanation.surface: A migrating bird's home crossing a region of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is the region of western Asia around the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: A male holding foreign currency, not according to plan

indicators.note: holding means the male word contains the currency

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A man carrying foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at random means done without any plan.

clue.text: Stop publications — they are bound to take extreme positions

definitions.text: they are bound to take extreme positions

parts.note: to end is to stop
papers are publications

explanation.surface: A call to shut down newspapers that are bound to be extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' means sewn into a book, and the 'extreme positions' are the front and back.
explanation.definitionFit: Endpapers are bound into a book at its very start and end.

clue.text: Layer at bottom of river placed like this

definitions.text: Layer at bottom of river placed like this

indicators.note: at bottom of tells us, in a down clue, that the layer word goes under the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a ply is a layer

explanation.surface: Describes sediment settled on a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying at the bottom of a river is placed deeply.

clue.text: Composer gets legal judgment without court

indicators.note: without means the court letters are removed

parts.note: a verdict is a legal judgment

explanation.surface: A composer wins a ruling out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer.

clue.text: Person of unusual beauty, in a sense

definitions.meaning: someone strikingly lovely may be called a ...
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Someone beautiful in some respect.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunning person is called a vision, and sight is one of the senses.

clue.text: See 11 across
King Edward, for one, not altogether an art patron

indicators.note: not altogether means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and tater is slang for potato

explanation.surface: A king who was only partly a sponsor of art.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety, not the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Tate, sugar magnate, founded the Tate Gallery as a patron of art.

clue.text: Having changed habits, installing new shrub

indicators.note: installing means the rearranged letters take in the extra one
changed means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Having changed one's ways, one plants a new bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' suggests behaviour or clothing, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is another name for wormwood, a shrubby plant.

clue.text: Sam's wife Sally, perhaps

parts.note: Uncle Sam's wife would be a relation of the same kind, and Sally of the fairground target game also bears that title

explanation.surface: Asks whether Sam is married to a Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam's partner would be his female counterpart; Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing at a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The female partner of an uncle is an aunt, and Aunt Sally is the fairground figure.

clue.text: See 11 across
Soldier with you and me sounding bitter

indicators.note: sounding means the pieces are said aloud

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, and us is you and me

explanation.surface: A soldier in company with us sounding resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of bitter resentment.
